content_voiceover: This diagram maps each heme biosynthesis enzyme to its corresponding porphyria when deficient, a classic boards exercise. The pathway starts in mitochondria, glycine plus succinyl-CoA form ALA via ALA synthase, feedback-inhibited by hemin. In the cytosol, ALA dehydratase deficiency causes ALA dehydratase porphyria, very rare. Porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency causes acute intermittent porphyria, AIP, the most important to know, autosomal dominant, roughly one to two per twenty-thousand, causing neurovisceral attacks and psychiatric symptoms, but no photosensitivity, since the accumulating ALA and PBG aren't photoactive. Uroporphyrinogen III synthase deficiency causes congenital erythropoietic porphyria. Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency causes porphyria cutanea tarda, the most common porphyria overall, about one in ten-thousand, presenting with photosensitivity, not neurovisceral disease. Further down, coproporphyrinogen oxidase and protoporphyrinogen oxidase deficiencies cause hereditary coproporphyria and variegate porphyria, both mixed neurovisceral and cutaneous. Finally, ferrochelatase deficiency causes erythropoietic protoporphyria. Notice lead poisoning inhibits both ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase, which is why lead poisoning can mimic parts of this pathway.
keypoints: ALA synthase = rate-limiting, feedback-inhibited by hemin
PBG deaminase deficiency -> AIP (dominant, neurovisceral + psychiatric, no photosensitivity)
UROD deficiency -> PCT (most common porphyria, photosensitive)
Ferrochelatase deficiency -> EPP; lead inhibits ALA dehydratase & ferrochelatase
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know two porphyrias cold. Acute intermittent porphyria, from porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency, is dominant and causes neurovisceral attacks with psychiatric symptoms but no photosensitivity. Porphyria cutanea tarda, from uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency, is the most common porphyria and causes photosensitivity without neurovisceral disease. Also remember lead poisoning inhibits both ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase, mimicking this pathway.
